reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered paragraphs are unchanged from the originals.

The cited text supports compliance: Section 2.7 is a standard license-use/reverse-engineering restriction on the Software, not a covenant limiting Corio's business or its ability to buy or build competing products.

The 'Corio Market Segment' (<$1B customers) and 'Territory' (North America) definitions operate as scope-of-grant limitations on the license Commerce One gives us, not as prohibitions on our operating any business or reselling other vendors' products; treating them as a non-compete and redlining the negotiated license scope would be over-flagging.
Section 13.6 expressly preserves each party's independent development rights and the covenant not to sue is mutual, reinforcing the absence of any restrictive covenant binding the customer.

Deterministic check ('no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains') passes, consistent with the preferred position of no non-compete or field-of-use restriction; the rationale accurately flags the field-of-use scoping as license-scope context rather than a deviation.
